report:
Reviewed all three implementation entries and eight associated tests for handle_ownership. Requirements are owner-relative Ptr/Slice interpretation, explicit structural transfer across stash boundaries, and completed output ownership independent of source CST/imported query stashes. Captured storage-guide and architectural rationale explicitly distinguish debug ownership checks from release reliance on the invariant; this is not a claim of release-time owner branding.

sage-stash::validate_stash_id checks the debug handle tag against the owning stash before pointer/slice indexing. Both indexing paths additionally validate entry type, including release builds. Handles contain an entry index (plus debug owner tag), and equality/hash alone do not establish cross-stash identity. StashCopy for Ptr reads the source value, recursively copies it, and allocates in the target; Slice recursively copies every element into a target slice. Stashed::copy_into supplies its own source owner. Self-contained StashDirect values are copied directly, rather than confusing database identities with stash handles.

The macro implementation generate_stash_copy_body recursively invokes StashCopy for every named/tuple struct field and every named/tuple enum field, handles unit cases, and rejects unions. This makes derived compound copies traverse nested handles instead of copying their numerical indices. finalize_typed_body creates a fresh stash and structurally copies root, locals and body. BodyFinalizer resolves source egraph representatives/expression slots and recursively rebuilds type, alias, trait/call argument, expression, statement, pattern, field and arm edges in the destination, using memo tables to preserve repeated references. Captured Const and TokenTree definitions confirm the directly retained array length/token fields are self-contained values or database handles, not hidden stash pointers. The review concerns copy ownership, not authored expression-checking semantics.

All eight tests have meaningful visible expectations. cross_stash_ptr_same_type_panics_in_debug and cross_stash_slice_panics_in_debug require owner mismatch only under debug assertions; they intentionally do not assert owner rejection in release. cross_stash_ptr_wrong_type and cross_stash_slice_with_different_element_type_is_rejected require debug owner mismatch and release type mismatch. copy_into_compound checks both nested Point values through copied pointers; copy_into_with_slice checks copied elements. copied_nested_handles_survive_source_drop_and_destination_growth uses a different destination entry layout, drops the source-owned tree, grows the destination by 4096 allocations, then checks values, slice length and repeated-handle equality. This exercises structural copying even without debug owner tags. finalized_nested_body_owns_resolved_and_imported_types_after_sources_drop constructs an imported bool and source inference/slot/tuple tree, finalizes it, asserts the original source remains unchanged, drops egraph/source/imported storage, and traverses the destination to assert concrete bool types, literal values, spans, repeated resolved children and empty locals.

Captured fixture type declarations ensure those nested fields are actual Ptr/Slice members with generated copying, not opaque helper assertions. Coverage is focused unit/constructed completed-body evidence, not an exhaustive audit of all future tree variants or every compiler query. Within the documented debug/release ownership contract, the set covers the specified pointer/slice misuse, recursive copying and source-independent output scenarios. No TODO/N/A entries are associated here. No code changes or tests executed in this review; commands were fresh review start/read and source inspection before recording. No requested edits.
